SMTO-AUT-0026 — The Google sign-in ended without giving permission

GUID: d249e8d4-3f73-5f9e-9d1f-3169950b4392
Slug: google-authorization-cancelled
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • Google came back without approving access, for example because Cancel was selected or Google refused the request. SMTO got no new access and saved nothing from this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Decide whether you still want SMTO to have this Google access. If not, you're done. SMTO treats a cancelled or refused sign-in as a no and keeps nothing from it.
  2. If you do want it, ask SMTO for a new Google connection and approve the access Google lists on its page. This sign-in can't be resumed; only a new, deliberate approval gives SMTO access.
  3. If Google showed a message saying the app or access is blocked, send that message to whoever manages your Google account or organization. Google can refuse access by policy, and SMTO can't change that from its side.

What success looks like

  • If you started a new connection, the Google sign-in tab says your email is connected; otherwise SMTO simply doesn't have this access.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve access you don't want just to make this message go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Google browser callback carried an error after its matching state was consumed, so consent did not complete and nothing was saved.

What this means

  • The browser callback supplied an error after the matching authorization state was consumed; consent did not complete successfully. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The browser callback supplied an error after the matching authorization state was consumed; consent did not complete successfully.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether consent was deliberately declined or the provider reported an error, without reusing the consumed callback.

How to fix it

  • No server-side repair is required: the provider returned an error parameter (for example a user cancellation or a policy refusal) and the pending state was consumed. Start a new auth.google_connect consent only if the access is still wanted; if Google refuses every time, review the app's OAuth consent screen and any Google Workspace admin restrictions in Google Cloud Console.
  • Start consent again only if the requested access is still needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Start consent again only if the requested access is still needed.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly requested consent completes only if the user still intends that access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
